column2: Two new essays: Before the State, and How Songs Travel
column3: Research Series 07 asks how peoples lived without kings, from the Natufians and the Jōmon to the five living cultures that have outlived the states around them; 08 follows the 300 songs of Songs in History from the oldest tablets to the anthems, the tunes that branched into other nations' songs, and what states and movements made of them. Also new in Songs in History: Chollima on the Wing, the song of North Korea's Chollima Movement, and an entry for the movement itself.

column2: Songs of states and causes, and a dozen new features
column3: Sixty-six songs of states, parties and causes join Songs in History, from Rule, Britannia! and the Soviet anthem to the songs of Mao's China, North Korea, fascist Italy and the Hong Kong protests, each told as history. New: compare any two profiles side by side; a timeline view of the profiles; Where Is This Song From?, a daily song game; Born on This Day on the home page; Next to read; search inside the songs' words; the encyclopedia filtered by era and by picture; levels in My Passport; an On This Day card for other websites; reading paths read aloud as a guided tour; this What's new page; worksheets on the cultures and the songs; and the Epic of Gilgamesh now in Sumerian.
column4: The songs|/songs/ ; Compare two profiles|/compare ; The song game|/games#songq ; Worksheets|/teachers/

column2: Encyclopedia, offline reading, Meanwhile in the world
column3: 229 songs and 16 forms of government have entries of their own; entries and songs show what else was happening in the world that year; the home page has a Song of the Day; pages already read open without a connection, and the site can be added to a phone's home screen.

The culture archive grows from 15 to 45, with more of Asia and South Asia: Mehrgarh, the Vedic civilisation, Sangam-age Tamilakam, Jōmon, Yayoi, Liangzhu, Sanxingdui, Dong Son, the Ainu and more, from the Natufians and the Yamnaya to the Taíno, the Thule people and the Māori.

column2: The Epic of Gilgamesh, and better performances
column3: The Epic of Gilgamesh joins Songs in History with Peter Pringle's performance in Sumerian; eight songs have a better recording.

233 songs handed down through history, from a Sumerian hymn to songs of the Cold War: their story, their words in the original, romanized and in English where they are in the public domain, and a sung performance.

Twenty forms of government, from absolute monarchy to the city-state and colonial rule, each with how it works, its history, its strengths and weaknesses; a hub that compares them and lets you design a state; and an essay, Who Should Rule?
218 inventions and discoveries in eleven lanes, from stone tools to the World Wide Web: what each built on, what it led to and who made it first.
How thirty societies ranked their people, ruler to enslaved, with how many stood on each rung; be born into one by chance, compare two, or put the ranks in order in a game.

column2: Thirty cultures and movements, speeches and paths
column3: The first cultures and movements, 138 new encyclopedia entries, twenty more great speeches and ten more reading paths.

column2: Rise and Fall Race, Flashcards, Who Said It?
column3: Race empires through the centuries, learn with flashcards, guess who said a quotation, test yourself at the end of a profile, and see everything you have read on My timeline.
